Why city trees matter

Urban trees reduce summer heat by shading streets and buildings while also releasing water vapour through their leaves. These effects can lower local temperatures and make outdoor spaces more comfortable during hot weather.

Trees also intercept rainfall, provide habitat for wildlife, and can improve the experience of walking through a neighbourhood. Their benefits depend on species, health, placement, and long-term maintenance.

Related story: ten gardens to visit this weekend and five products our editors recommend.

Researchers therefore assess urban forests as infrastructure as well as living ecosystems. Cities need enough space, soil, water, and maintenance if newly planted trees are to survive and deliver benefits over many years.
